line: The Korea Baduk Association. Rows of boards, and children who have given their whole lives to them.
Jang Geu-rae came here at eleven. He is eighteen now. This is his last chance to turn professional.
Last round. Win, and you're in. Lose, and you've aged out.
beats.speaker: ex

line: It wasn't talent, he tells himself. It wasn't the half-points, or the part-time jobs, or that there was never pocket money.
It wasn't that his father died, or that his mother took to her bed.
Those reasons hurt too much. So he'll say it was this: I didn't try hard enough.

He leaves baduk. A sponsor finds him a job; when his colleagues learn where he came from, they mock it, and he quits. He does his military service. Eight months after he comes out, the same sponsor calls the president of a trading company.
One International, a general trading company in Jongno. Interns in new suits wait for passes that have their names on them.
Jang Geu-rae? You're not on my list. Oh, here: the president's office sent your name down separately.
beats.speaker: desk

line: Everyone else got in with a degree and a test. He got in with a phone call. He knows how that looks.
The gates open for him like for anyone else.
Sales Team 3. Seventh floor. Section head Oh Sang-sik.
beats.speaker: desk

line: You're mine? Kim, he's yours. Show him where things are and don't let him touch anything that ships.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Assistant manager Kim Dong-sik. Welcome. You'll sit by me.
beats.speaker: kd

line: If there's a light I'm meant to keep lit here, I'll answer for it. Whatever light I'm given.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Oh's eyes are red. He hasn't slept, by the look of them. He doesn't look up again.
Can I borrow your glue stick? Mine's dry.
beats.speaker: sh

line: Kim Seok-ho, an intern from another firm's programme: married young, a child at home, the best translator of them all. He works fast. A page of Sales 3's comes away stuck to the back of his.
An hour later the director comes up from the lobby holding a waybill. It was on the floor by the gates, where anyone could read it.
Whose is this? A customer's shipment, on the floor of my lobby! Who had it last?
beats.speaker: dir

line: Every intern is made to stand. Every eye goes to the parachute.
The one nobody tested. Of course.
beats.speaker: dir

line: Oh Sang-sik says nothing to Jang. He takes the lift down to the lobby.
Torn from the waybill's back: a strip with glue on it, and a name in an intern's careful hand. Kim Seok-ho.
Oh goes up and has a word with the director, and Kim Seok-ho is called in. Nobody says sorry to Jang. Oh doesn't either.
If it fell here, there's more of it. Bins first.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: Assistant manager Park Jong-gi from IT sales carries a resignation letter in his jacket. On the roof, Jang told him he admired his patience. Park heard something else: that someone thought he could be a hunter.
So he brought Jang along to a client.
Through the door they hear the client's staff. They're laughing about Park: how far they can push him, what he'll swallow next.
We'll be revising the terms. All of them. I'll send the paper tomorrow.
beats.speaker: pj

line: The client's president stares at him. So does Jang.
The client's president has come to One International in person, angry, and wants Park's head.
Jang writes four words on a slip and passes it under the table: Be irresponsible, sir. Blame the junior.
The deception was mine. Not his. I'm the one who misled you.
beats.speaker: pj

line: Nobody punishes Park. The client goes home with nothing to say. Park comes up to the roof afterwards to thank Jang, and means it.
Everyone has their own game of baduk. He played his.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Deputy general manager Sun Ji-young keeps work and home in two sealed rooms. Tonight they've run into each other.
The daycare closes at seven. My meeting doesn't. I hate asking. I'm asking.
beats.speaker: sun

line: Somi. Five. She'll be the last one there. Tell her Mummy's sorry.
beats.speaker: sun

line: We'll go. Jang Geu-rae, you're coming.
beats.speaker: ahn

line: Ahn Young-yi: the intern everyone talks about. Political science, two companies behind her already, never a word out of place.
Seven o'clock. One by one the other children's parents come through the gate. Somi watches every one of them, and every one of them isn't hers.
Somi? Your mum sent us. She's sorry she's late.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: They walk her home between them. Neither of them says much. It is the first time they've been anywhere together.
The internship ends with a test. The interns are paired; each pair presents a business plan to a panel.
Jang draws Han Seok-yul: the loudest intern on the floor, who once ordered Jang around until Jang asked how old he was. It turned out Han is a year older.
Everything that matters happens on the shop floor. My father, my uncles: factory men. Paper doesn't make anything.
beats.speaker: han

line: Then you talk. I'll make the paper.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: On the frame strip Cho Hunhyun, eight points of komi against him, considers the lower side.
Cho broke White's lower side at the cost of his own shape, because eight points of komi left him no choice.
...and that's why the site comes first. Thank you.
beats.speaker: han

line: Ahn Young-yi's pair goes next. It is so clean that a panelist laughs.
Is she the president's daughter, or one of ours undercover?
beats.speaker: ms_examiner

line: Jang Baek-gi's pair presents safe numbers, neatly compiled, and is told it has no vision.
Last task. Sell your partner something. Partner, you may buy or refuse.
beats.speaker: ms_examiner

line: Office slippers. An office worker's combat boots: the shoes you fight in all day.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Your boots are for a shop floor. This floor is a shop floor too. You've been fighting on it for two months.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: ...I won't buy them. But I think I've been looking down on this floor.
beats.speaker: ms_han

line: The results. Ahn Young-yi, first overall. Jang Baek-gi, hired: the steel team. Han Seok-yul, hired. Kim Seok-ho, hired, to the group's head office.
Jang Geu-rae, hired. On a two-year contract.
On the first morning Oh takes his new people to a memorial for laid-off workers before he takes them to their desks. He doesn't explain why.
The resources team. Ahn's seniors have decided she is too sure of herself, and too good at it. Finance has sent their plan back.
Nobody on the team will go and ask why. Ahn goes.
You're the new one. You walked in here without your section head.
beats.speaker: ksj

line: The plan was sent back without a reason, ma'am. I'd like the reason.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: Kim Seon-ju, head of finance: the only woman at her level in the building.
The reason is that you're a first-year who thinks a good plan is enough. Go back to your team.
beats.speaker: ksj

line: Ahn goes back to her team with the plan, and the lesson.
Sales 3's item, crude from Iran to Turkey, dies on an EU embargo. The team's little good-luck rite didn't help.
You were a trainee at the Baduk Association. Seven years. I looked it up.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Because a company's no different from a baduk board. Here.
beats.speaker: kd

line: He sets four stones on the desk in a ring around an empty point: Oh, himself, Jang, and the team.
Us. If we hold together we win. Look, we've already made one.
beats.speaker: kd

line: On the frame strip, Cho's group in the centre has no eyes yet.
Cho played it slack on purpose: he chose to settle his group, because living meant winning.
One eye. It's still not alive. Misaeng.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Later that month: division head Kim Bu-ryeon keeps his name off Sales 3's China report, then puts it back on once the report looks good. Another team takes their rare-earth idea whole. Oh Sang-sik gets a nosebleed at his desk, an IV drip on his own, and a box of dried eel from Kim Bu-ryeon, who tells him a father who wrecks his health is no use to anyone.
TEU, surcharges, Ramadan schedules. Every sentence in the office has a word in it Jang doesn't know.
Every morning there's a sheet on his desk: three questions, in Kim Dong-sik's handwriting. Nobody mentions it.
Middle East shipping. A report, by Friday. Don't pretend you know. Find out.
beats.speaker: kd

line: Oh reads it, corrects it in red, and hands it back. The next morning it is pinned up by the copier, laminated.
Section head Park Jong-sik joins Sales 3: once the steel team's ace and its Middle East hand, now the man nobody else wanted. Kim Bu-ryeon sent him, on the advice of Oh's old rival.
He plays billiards in the afternoons. He calls Jang the high-school parachute to his face.
And he stands too close to Shin Da-in, a young contract worker, every day, and says things to her that she pretends not to hear.
Da-in, you should smile more. Doesn't cost anything.
beats.speaker: pk

line: Da-in. Has he done this before? Every day?
beats.speaker: ms_sun

line: Your new section head is harassing a contract worker on my floor. I'm telling you because you're his team head. I'll tell the next person up if I have to.
beats.speaker: ms_sun

line: He does. He tells Park, in front of the team, that he can't work with him.
Left to find his own business, Park comes back with one: used cars to Jordan, through a Korean supplier called Baekjin Trading.
Look at this margin. Nobody makes that on used cars. Somebody's taking a cut.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Oh takes it to Kim Bu-ryeon, who signed off on the deal himself. Kim Bu-ryeon reads it twice.
Kim Dong-sik and Jang go to Baekjin Trading to see the supplier for themselves. Park Jong-sik is already there.
Sales 3. Thorough. Go on, ask them anything.
beats.speaker: pk

line: The staff answer every question the same way, in the same words, as if they'd learned them that morning.
They were told what to say. We can't prove it.
beats.speaker: kd

line: The audit team has been through everything and found nothing they can use. They're packing up.
Even in a game that's lost, there's a move you want to play. Let me play one.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: ICB, the Jordanian buyer, is all local staff on paper. When I called them, someone in the room was speaking Korean. Call them now.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: The auditor dials Amman. A man answers. In Korean, until he catches himself.
The signatory on every ICB document, Muhammad Indira, is a Korean called Park Sang-jun.
Park, Park, Park. Half the board is called Park.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: You wanted Park Jong-sik's family? The steel team keeps everything. Here.
beats.speaker: bg

line: James Park, director of ICB, is Park Jong-sik. Park Sang-jun is the son of Baekjin's president. Baekjin's president is Park's uncle.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Both ends of the deal. All family.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Not yet. I haven't put it together. ICB's registration is on the audit room's table; my notes from the call to ICB are on my desk in Sales 3. Then link them on the audit board, from the bag or the audit room's table.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: In 2008 I brought in a hundred million dollars of steel to Jordan. Alone. And what did I get for it? A team dinner on the director's card.
beats.speaker: pk

line: You lot eat the money, and I'm supposed to go home happy with my salary?
beats.speaker: pk

line: He leaves after a meeting with the executive vice president. The police come later.
Responsibility falls upward. Kim Bu-ryeon is moved to an affiliate, One Aluminium. A managing director resigns. Before he goes, Kim Bu-ryeon finds Oh, who blames himself, and tells him he did right.
Oh Sang-sik is made deputy general manager, and Sales 3 gets a bonus, and a name around the building: the team that informs on its own.
Nobody gets to say we didn't follow procedure.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Chuseok. The relatives' flat is full of cousins with degrees and uncles with opinions.
They ask about his job. Contract, he says. They stop asking, and start talking about him as if he'd left the room.
He goes out on the landing. Through the kitchen door he hears his mother, defending him to her own sisters, in tears.
Don't forget it. I'm my mother's pride. Not a son who falls short.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: After the holiday Sales 3 gets Park's replacement, section head Cheon Gwan-ung: ordinary, a heavy drinker, wary of a team that informs. When he needles Kim Dong-sik over it, Oh shuts him down: you came here to work, not to play games. Cheon apologises.
And Jang proposes reviving the Jordan used-car deal that Park's fraud killed: clean, this time, to show the company can.
Kim Dong-su was Oh's senior once. He quit years ago. His pizza shop is being crushed by the big mart's pizza across the road.
Your old clients, Sang-sik. A word from you. I'm not asking for nothing.
beats.speaker: kds

line: I can't take it. Go and see Kim Seok-man at Hangang Trading. He'll hear you out.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: They say the company's a battlefield? Outside, it's hell. Don't you quit. Not till they push you out.
beats.speaker: kds

line: Back at the office, the team has a briefing to give the president. Oh hands Jang the seating notes.
Every seat set, every pen squared. The last rehearsal goes perfectly, and Oh frowns all the way through it.
It's tidy. Tidy doesn't sell a deal the board already hates. We need to shake it.
beats.speaker: oh

line: On the frame strip, the game turns.
The move that turned the flow of the game.
Approved. Who did the legwork? The youngest. What did he do?
beats.speaker: pr

line: It was his idea, sir. All of it started with him.
beats.speaker: oh

line: That evening Jang looks at his card. Contract. He reads the word twice.
If I just keep doing as I do... I'll become a regular, won't I?
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Here. A hundred thousand won. Buy something and sell it. Come back and tell me what you learned.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Every seat as it's written on the notes: the president's water, the executive's tea, the division head's coffee. Then we rehearse.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: I went to the Baduk Association first. They told me they'd buy anything I brought, out of pity or kindness, and asked if I'd call that doing my job.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Then the street. The old man at the corner shop sold more dried squid while I was talking than I sold all day.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: You can't climb stairs that have no first step. And you can't sell like you're running away.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Not yet. The market stalls on Jongno sell stock; the street's full of people to sell it to.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: At a group meeting at head office, Ahn's proposal was chosen over resources team 3's. Her department head had been backing team 3, to build his own camp.
Who told you to embarrass this department in front of head office? Who do you think you are?
beats.speaker: ma

line: Young-yi. My promotion's this round. Please. Just drop it.
beats.speaker: ab

line: ...I'll withdraw it. Team 3's plan will go forward.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: She stays up there until the lunch hour is over.
She drinks too fast, and Jang lets her. Then she puts her head down on the table and cries.
Her father is an army officer. He wanted sons. Prizes, class president, head of the student council: he never looked.
When he heard his daughter was on an executive track, he asked about her salary, and then about loans in her name. When she said no, he hit her.
So I cut him off. And left. And came here. And today I did what I was told.
beats.speaker: ms_ahn

line: You're allowed to like yourself a bit more. You don't have to earn it every day.
beats.speaker: jg

line: A few days later the department head is dressed down himself, by head office, for blocking the plan they had liked. Jang buys her a necklace. She wears it. He doesn't notice.
I've been promoted. We don't need two salaries. You can stop now. Stay home with her.
beats.speaker: hb

line: I'm not only Somi's mother. I'm a person who works. I want to be seen as one.
beats.speaker: sun

line: They talk until late. In the end the housework is no longer something he helps with. It is something he has to do.
At the office, the rumour that she's leaving is already going round. Somebody says: women.
After Jordan, the executive vice president takes Sales 3 into his own line, and gives them his long-running China business on handsome terms.
Oh sees what that patronage could mean: a regular contract for Jang. He sees what else it could mean, too.
Nobody here thinks we've caught a golden rope. Nobody. And keep a copy of everything.
beats.speaker: oh

line: Oh and the others are out. The phone on the team's desk rings: the company's man in China.
Is this Sales 3? Our partner's asking about the arrangements. The usual gifts, the relationships. What do you want me to tell them?
beats.speaker: ms_chinarep

line: I'll lay it out. The gifts, the guanxi: we'll need to understand exactly what's been going to whom, and why.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: He means to help. In China, it lands as an alarm. Within days the Chinese partner tips off One International's audit department, and a nine-year business comes apart.
A fight between departments is the leader's game. Yours is your own. Play your own.
beats.speaker: oh

line: The division head has spent the evening pouring drinks for Oh. Oh goes straight from the table to the executive's office.
On the frame strip, Cho's big group must find a way to live.
Cho's way to live with the group.
Were those gifts relationships, sir, or were they the company's money walking out the door?
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: It comes out in the audit: the Chinese partner had been using the executive's ambition, and skimming One International's real profit for years.
Thank you for ending it quietly.
beats.speaker: ex

line: He is made president of One Global Service, an unlisted affiliate nobody visits.
Jang is crying. He did it out of love for the team, and it doesn't matter.
I understand. And that's the end of it. Regret it today. Only today.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: A contract worker with a high-school certificate. Converting him to regular. Is there a way?
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: There's no precedent. I'd say it'll probably be difficult.
beats.speaker: hr

line: Sales 3 is alone now. Kim Dong-su comes back with an offer: a small company of their own.
Oh thinks about his four sons, about chicken versus eel. His wife tells him: buy everything at the staff discount, and stay till the bonus.
People are everything. That's all a company is.
beats.speaker: ms_oh

line: He resigns, and asks Kim Bu-ryeon to come in with them. Cheon Gwan-ung is left holding the team.
Two years. The contract ends on a weekday. Jang hands in his card and walks out through the gates.
Looking back, the building is already cold, as though it had never been his.
Three weeks later. A narrow street, an office up a flight of stairs. Oh Sang-sik's new trading company has hired its first regular employee: Jang Geu-rae.
On the frame strip, 144 moves. Nie Weiping's stones press on Cho's centre.
Black 145. White's five stones in the centre can't escape now. Nie Weiping resigns. Cho Hunhyun is the first world champion in Korean baduk.
Kim Dong-sik. I've quit too. Is the post still open?
beats.speaker: kd

line: I got here first. So you're the junior.
beats.speaker: ms_jang

line: Later, Jang is in Amman, on the phone to his boss in Seoul. Back at One International, under a new team head, Cheon Gwan-ung stays.
As a breadwinner, as a father, I'm colourless. That's my colour.
beats.speaker: ms_cheon
